subject: Biotechnology
title: Synthetic Biology Preview
description: A micro-lesson that makes Synthetic Biology Preview usable.

hook.text: What if you could write DNA from scratch — designing organisms that never existed in nature?

buildup.text: Synthetic biology treats genes like software — writing, compiling, and debugging genetic programs.

discovery.text: Craig Venter created the first synthetic cell in 2010 — booting up a bacterium with lab-made DNA.

twist.text: Synbio startups now program yeast to make fragrances, spider silk, and even meat proteins — no farms needed.

climax.text: The iGEM competition lets students build new organisms from standardized DNA parts — biology's open-source movement.

punchline.text: Synthetic biology writes life from code — biotech's next chapter.

quiz.question: What did Craig Venter achieve in 2010?
options: He cloned the first mammal from an adult cell
He created the first cell running entirely on lab-synthesized DNA
He discovered CRISPR in bacterial immune systems

details.summary: Synthetic biology applies engineering principles to biology, designing and building new biological systems from standardized genetic parts. It goes beyond genetic engineering by constructing entirely new pathways and circuits rather than modifying existing ones.
details.whyItMatters: Synthetic biology is the cutting edge of biotechnology, enabling the design of organisms with capabilities that do not exist in nature. It is driving innovations in medicine, materials, computing, and environmental remediation.
takeaways: Synthetic biology designs new biological systems from standardized genetic parts
It applies engineering principles like modularity and abstraction to biology
Applications range from living therapeutics to biological computers to new materials

faq.question: How does synthetic biology differ from traditional genetic engineering?
faq.answer: Genetic engineering typically moves existing genes between organisms. Synthetic biology designs and builds entirely new genetic sequences, circuits, and pathways from scratch using standardized parts, much like engineering constructs electronic circuits from components.

faq.question: What are some real-world applications of synthetic biology?
faq.answer: Engineered microbes produce antimalarial drugs, fragrances, and biofuels. Synthetic gene circuits create living biosensors that detect toxins. Programmed bacteria target tumors as living therapeutics. DNA is used as a data storage medium for digital information.
